reader.requirement: At --std 85, SUBTRACT format 3 must accept CORR and CORRESPONDING interchangeably with identical results, including ROUNDED and the SIZE ERROR phrases, while a word that is neither (CORRES) does not select format 3.

edition-consulted.switches: CORR and CORRESPONDING reserved; both rows true at all four editions
ROUNDED MODE IS refused below 2014 (a phrase of the statement, not of this rule)

reader.edition-search: grep CORR/CORRESPONDING over the grammar (one alternative '(CORRESPONDING | CORR)'), CorrespondingBinder (sub.CORRESPONDING() is not null || sub.CORR() is not null) and ReservedWords.Table.cs
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers the word equivalence; this run adds ROUNDED, ON SIZE ERROR / NOT ON SIZE ERROR, subordinate group, OCCURS and FILLER exclusion, and ADD CORR in the same program

probes.printed: CORR 0H05zzz5579 NSE1; CORRESPONDING 0H05zzz5579 NSE1; ADD CORR 0I15zzz5599; ADD CORRESP 0I15zzz5599
probes.expected: identical lines: A = 10 - 1.6 rounded = +8 (0H, trailing overpunch), B = |5 - 10| = 05, C, OCCURS T and FILLER untouched, SUBG.D = 7; NOT ON SIZE ERROR taken

probes.printed: error COBOL0844 (group SRC not a numeric operand) and COBOL1675 (resultant DST is a group)
probes.expected: CORRES is not the abbreviation: read as format 1 with group operands, refused

probes.printed: error COBOL0803: ROUNDED MODE IS requires COBOL-2014 (targeting COBOL-85)
probes.expected: ROUNDED MODE is not a 1985 phrase: refused

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.6.26.3 SR4  (6.26.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR4
OK  §1985:VI.6.6.3 SR4  (6.6.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR4

reader.notes: CORR and CORRESPONDING are separate tokens joined in one grammar alternative and tested together in the binder, so both spellings reach the same Bind(CorrVerb.Subtract, ...). The probe outputs are byte-identical between the spellings and match the 1985 general rules.

refuter.evidence: refute-1985-159/sub1.cob at --std 85 (runs/sub1-001): lowercase 'subtract corr' and mixed-case 'Subtract Corresponding' give identical 'LOW 09501}008 09501}008' (A 100-5=95, signed B 10-20=-10 overpunched, nested SG.C 9-1=8, per GR3); with SIZE ERROR phrases both spellings take NOT ON SIZE ERROR and give '00201}' (unsigned A=|3-5|=2). Refusals at --std 85: CORR with two receivers (format 3 has one identifier-2 at 1985) COBOL0307 (sub-bad1); CORRESPONDING ... GIVING COBOL2269 (sub-bad2); two sending groups COBOL5506 (sub-bad3); a literal after CORR COBOL5506 (sub-bad4). cite.py: OK §1985:VI.6.26.3 SR4 'CORR is an abbreviation for CORRESPONDING'; OK §1985:VI.6.26.4 GR3. No 1985-only spelling exists, and no later-edition form of the CORR keyword to refuse beyond the reader's ROUNDED MODE probe.
